title: pvVisItVASPCHGCARReader
body:
## pvVisItVASPCHGCARReader

Reads VASP (Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package) charge-density files (CHGCAR or CHG; the reader matches names starting with CHG): the density on the unit-cell grid becomes a point array "charge", with atom and unit-cell meshes alongside. ParaView's pvVASPAnimationReader and pvVASPTessellationReader read different VASP files, not CHGCAR. One file supplies every time step the format stores.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The first mesh is "atoms"; select "mesh" to get the charge-density grid.
- No rescaling is applied: "charge" holds the values as stored in the file (VASP writes density times cell volume).
- Name the arrays you need in PointArrays and CellArrays: the VisIt bridge starts with every variable unselected, so omitting them normally gives geometry without fields.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue and has not run a native acceptance check for this reader; check meshes, arrays and times on your own data.

Native constructor: `VisItVASPCHGCARReader`. Identity: `sources/VisItVASPCHGCARReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrays` | Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from VASP CHGCAR data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The VASP CHGCAR plugin declares its variables node-centred, so this list normally stays empty. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileName` | Path of the single VASP CHGCAR file to read (CHG*); the reader takes every time step the format stores from it. Use an absolute path; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). The file is usually named CHGCAR or CHG (no extension). Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Materials` | Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The VASP CHGCAR plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Meshes` | Names of the VASP CHGCAR meshes to read. Each selected mesh becomes one named block of the multiblock output and unlisted meshes are skipped. The CHGCAR plugin reports the atom point mesh "atoms" first and the charge-density grid "mesh" second, so by default only the atoms are read. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PointArrays` | Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from VASP CHGCAR data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. For VASP CHGCAR data these are the node-centred "charge" density on the grid. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvVisItVASPCHGCARReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
